publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'D'.pdf
publications.explanation:
The intended choice is the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in the same period. The formula is: maternal mortality ratio = (maternal deaths ÷ live births) × 100,000. This distinguishes the 100,000 denominator from the 10,000 distractor. The definition includes deaths related to or aggravated by pregnancy or its management during pregnancy or within 42 days after it ends; accidental or incidental causes are excluded.

The question calls this a “rate,” but the live-birth denominator defines a maternal mortality ratio. The technical maternal mortality rate uses women of reproductive age as its population at risk. [WHO definition](https://www.who.int/data/gho/indicator-metadata-registry/imr-details/26) · [UN indicator guidance](https://millenniumindicators.un.org/wiki/spaces/SDGeHandbook/pages/35291223/Indicator%2B3.1.1).
